answer: Charge every new agent a small refundable stake before it can trade. A free identity can be copied by the thousands, but a stake turns each copy into a real expense. saffron gives a good picture: each flower yields only a few threads, so faking a large harvest takes work. The network can also watch the pulse of activity across accounts; identities moving in lockstep from one source get flagged. Reputation then grows slowly, like moss across a tundra, so a fresh swarm cannot buy trust overnight. An attacker pays the stake, waits out the slow build, and risks losing the deposit when caught.
